# Independent audit: uniform planar three-cap overlap stability

Auditor: `minkowski_transfer`. Verdict: **PASS** for the complete source
`candidate 40c46f71889ea6fc`, including
its deficit-localization Section 6. This is a proof audit, not a numerical
test or an assertion of a mixed-integer depth bound.

## Normalization and compactness

The maximal inscribed triangle is attained on the compact set of vertex
triples and has positive area. Every choice of maximizing triangle can
be used. Replacing its i-th vertex by a point of the normalized body
gives the exact area ratio `|lambda_i|`, so `|lambda_i|<=1` and
`T subset K* subset conv{(1,1),(1,-1),(-1,1)}`. The latter containing
triangle is indeed the intersection of all three barycentric slabs.
The maximum-inscribed-area restriction survives Hausdorff limits by
approximating each of the three limiting vertices. Thus the normalized
body class is compact, contains a fixed full-dimensional triangle, and
requires no continuous selection of a maximizing triangle.

Unit cap normals and offsets clipped below at -2 range over a compact
parameter set. This clipping affects only full traces and preserves
their sets exactly. Positive cap area excludes offsets at or above 2.
Hausdorff convergence of the bodies and convergence of the nonzero unit
normals yield almost-everywhere convergence of both body and cap
indicators, with only convex boundaries and lines excluded. Dominated
convergence in the fixed bounding ball proves convergence of every area;
the denominator is bounded below by 1/2. The closed covering property
passes to the limit by approximating each point and selecting a repeated
cap index. All positive-minimum constraints therefore define a compact
class, including the harmless empty-class case.

## Equality limit and attained modulus

The equality-rigidity dependency was independently audited in
`historical context (not an accepted premise)`. Its positive-cap
hypothesis holds here. A triangular equality body in the normalized
class contains T and has area at most the area of T, so it equals T.
The three displayed normalized cap parameters are exactly the canonical
centroid vertex caps of T. The distance functional is continuous,
including its minimum over finitely many permutations. Consequently its
closed bad set is compact, and a nonempty bad set has a strictly positive
attained minimum of the normalized surplus. Taking half that minimum
gives the asserted strict conclusions even though the input surplus
inequality is non-strict. Empty bad sets and tau>1 are handled correctly.

## Tightening and deficit localization

For coordinatewise area loss, the functional
`F(A)=sum A-(3/4)min A` loses at least one quarter of the total loss.
The concurrent overlap theorem thus gives the exact annular bound
`E >= sum(A_i-A_i')/4`. It also gives the stated retained minimum
`tau V-4E >= tau V/2` when `E<=tau V/8`. This uses only the declared
positive-circuit tightening and does not assert such a tightening for
an arbitrary cover.

In Section 6 the selected global cap occurrences, including repetitions,
have total mass at most `3kB`; their restrictions to their owned fibers
have no larger sum. Local covering gives the lower bound M on that sum,
so `kB>=M/3` and the small-budget premise forces `delta<=1/9`.
For `0<eta<delta`, the coefficient `1/9-eta` is strictly positive.
Good fibers contribute at least `(4/9-eta)V_z` to the average of their
three cap areas. Every other fiber contributes at least `V_z/3`.
The nongood mass is at most `W_tau+E_tot/epsilon`; this remains a valid
upper bound when it exceeds M. Summation proves exactly

    kB >= (4/9-eta)M-(1/9-eta)(W_tau+E_tot/epsilon),

and combination with the stated small-budget assumption proves the
displayed localization coefficient without any lost factor of three.

No gap was found. The source correctly retains the missing global
arithmetic/deformation step and does not infer that either alternative
is impossible at a mixed-integer extremizer. No new computation is
needed for this compactness and finite-sum argument.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
